title: adaptive-kv-cache-calibration-with-error-bounded-int8-fp8-profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: evaluate operationally viable KV-cache quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8) with a calibration workflow that enforces an explicit accuracy budget while optimizing latency and cost. We aim to produce a rolloutable profile set + gating rules that keep relative quality regression <= 1% on automated benchmarks and human spot checks, while improving median latency and per-token cost.
acceptance_criteria: A set of calibrated INT8 and FP8 KV profiles that can be deployed behind rollout flags
Automated validation harness that compares PPL/EM/semantic-sim metrics vs FP16 baseline and reports per-workload deltas
SLO-compliant fallback: >99.5% of requests served under policy with no unexplained quality regressions
Design doc + PR merged: calibration pipeline, gating heuristics, rollout plan
updates: 2025-03-11: Kickoff meeting — agreed success metric = relative PPL delta <= 1% and 95p latency regression <= 5% vs FP16 when using tiered fallback.
2025-03-13: Implemented stratified sampling harness (short/medium/long sequences) and added synthetic drift injection to test calibration robustness.

2025-03-15: Ran first batch of runs on devpool (A100) — INT8 profile yields median latency -12% and 95p +9% on long sequences; FP8 yields median -18% and 95p +3% with 2.4% avg PPL regression on Llama-like suite.

2025-03-16: Observed noisy 95p behaviour due to mixing of kernel paths; created telemetry patch to report kernel-switch counts and KV cache hit patterns (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-quant-calib/pull/987).
2025-03-17: Engineering review — decided to prototype a sequence-length-aware gating layer that forces FP16 for >1024 tokens by default and allows mixed-precision for short/medium sequences.
2025-03-18: Ran mixed-precision tiered policy: median -14%, 95p +1.8%, avg PPL regression 0.9%; cost savings estimate ~22% vs baseline for typical traffic mix.

2025-03-19: Design review with PM/Runtime — agreed to add continuous calibration job that re-evaluates drift weekly and emits candidate profile updates; moved to In Progress for instrumentation and rollout testing.
2025-03-20: Blocker noted — calibration CI on multi-GPU nodes shows non-deterministic quant seeds leading to small metric variance; investigating deterministic quant seeds and RNG sync strategies.
results_summary: INT8 (per-layer symmetric) — median latency change: -12% overall; 95p on long sequences: +9%; avg PPL delta: +1.4%
FP8 (hybrid e4m3) — median latency change: -18% overall; 95p on long sequences: +3%; avg PPL delta: +2.4%
Tiered mixed-precision gating — median latency: -14%; 95p on long sequences: +1.8%; avg PPL delta: +0.9%; estimated cost savings: ~22%
Tail latency sensitivity correlated strongly with kernel-switch counts and KV-cache miss amplification on long prefixes.
notes_and_tradeoffs: INT8 gives better cost and stable median latency for many workloads but is more brittle on long-prefix KV cache accesses due to accumulated quantization error.
FP8 often achieves better raw latency improvement but shows larger accuracy variance on some decoder heads; careful per-layer calibration is required.
Tiered policy (sequence-length + workload-profile gating) seems to provide the best operational tradeoff — small quality regression, good cost wins, and bounded 95p impact.
Engineering complexity: rollout requires runtime support for per-request precision gating and fast fallback to FP16 without cold-cache penalties.
decisions: Prototype and iterate on tiered gating (short/medium use mixed-precision, long sequences default to FP16 unless explicitly allowed).
Add deterministic quant seeds to the calibration CI and re-run all baselines to reduce run-to-run variance.
Introduce weekly continuous calibration job that flags candidate profile degradations and generates alerts for manual review.
open_questions: What is the correct policy for bursty traffic where a sudden influx of long sequences might cause transient 95p regressions?
Should we include per-customer profile overrides in Dedicated/Private deployments to allow more aggressive quantization for tolerant workloads?
What cost threshold justifies the added runtime complexity for per-request precision switching?
next_steps: Fix deterministic-seed blocker and re-run full calibration sweep on staging cluster (owners: Liam/Omar) — target 2025-03-25.
Implement lightweight runtime hook for precision gating and fast FP16 fallback (owner: Diego) — target 2025-03-30.
Run A/B on 5% of traffic in Canary with tiered policy and automated quality monitors (owner: Mei) — target 2025-04-04.
Draft rollout playbook and customer communication templates for Dedicated/Private customers (owner: PM) — target 2025-04-04.
